items.q: Then we went to visit for a few days our friends Ronald Sweetman and his wife Jennifer... We had a swell time, and Jennifer and Ronald gave a party in our honour with 60 guests.

ctx.x: We gave a party at Max and Betty Jones' home for the Bruce Turner gang, and a few intimate friends. Max had been a well known critic and reporter for the Melody Maker musical magazine for many years. Bruce and the boys had a surprise gift for me which was a silver beer mug ingraved: "To Bill - the Guv'nor" from Bruce, Pete, Tony, Ray, Ron and Doug. That was a real sender for me and a gift I shall always cherish. Being called 'Guv'nor' in England is an honour in most cases, and these fellows were honouring me.

Then we went to visit for a few days our friends Ronald Sweetman and his wife Jennifer in a beautiful little town called Steyning in the Sussex country. Jennifer, by the way, is a very well known artist who paints under her maiden name of Jennifer Dickson. Their house was called 'Ellington house'. I hope you know why! We had a swell time, and Jennifer and Ronald gave a party in our honour with 60 guests.

During my stay in England, I met many English musicians that I had heard about, listened to on records but had never seen in person. To name a few: Danny Moss, who lived in Steyning, Sussex, where my friend Ronald Sweetman and his wife Jennifer lived, Ronnie Scott, owner of the famous club known under his name in London, Kenny Ball, a fine trumpet man and singer and many whose names I don't remember.
